title: Akhlaq in Dealings: Amanah and Birr al-Walidayn
summary: Worship is perfected through akhlaq, and at this age, the child grasps the meanings of amanah (trustworthiness) and truthfulness, as well as birr (righteousness toward parents). Teach him through example and story: amanah is safeguarding what he is entrusted with, birr is treating his parents well, being gentle with them, and obeying them in what is good; the Prophet ﷺ said: «There is no obedience in disobedience to Allah; obedience is only in what is good» (Sahih Muslim 1840), and truthfulness is a protection for people. Connect akhlaq to the love and pleasure of Allah, not just fear. Teach him the meaning of amanah and mercy through everyday situations and in language he understands, and have him practise one virtue in his daily behaviour. Praise his akhlaq when it appears. The child who links his worship to his akhlaq understands that religion is conduct, and that the closeness of the servant to his Lord is manifest in his truthfulness and rifq (gentleness) with people.
try_this: Today: Give your child a small amanah to keep for you (such as a pen or a key), ask him for it in the evening, and praise him for keeping it safe.
reflection_prompts: How does your child see the connection between his worship (his salah) and his akhlaq with people?
Which khuluq do you want your child to master this month, and how can you be his role model in it?
